clue.text: Officers sitting surprised a US general, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase before it is to be spoken and matched by ear

parts.note: to surprise is to catch out, so 'caught Marshall', George Marshall being a famous US general

explanation.surface: Some officers are startled by an American general who seems to be dropping by.
explanation.walkthrough: CAUGHT MARSHALL, said aloud, comes close to the name of the military trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tribunal is a panel of officers sitting in judgment on a serviceman.

clue.text: Noted form of hypocrisy a volunteer force understood

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Sanctimony from a reserve unit is understood to be a kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time volunteer reserve; 'Noted' means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral work with solos is a musical form written in notes.

clue.text: Remus, perhaps, taking the pledge?

definitions.meaning: ... Remus is the storyteller of the Joel Chandler Harris tales
a pawnbroker, old slang for whom is this relative, takes pledged goods

explanation.surface: Remus may be giving up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the pledge' looks like swearing off alcohol, but a pawnbroker takes pledges, and old slang calls one by this family title.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Remus is a storybook narrator, and in old slang a pawnbroker, who accepts pledged goods, goes by this kinship name.

clue.text: One hurt badly outside North Carolina club

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters wrap round the state abbreviation
badly says the letters of the phrase before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: NC is the postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: Someone was badly hurt outside a club in North Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes TRUHEON from ONE HURT, and 'outside' puts it round NC.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman's short baton is a kind of club.

clue.text: Such as Betsey Trotwood do not exist, it's said by some

indicators.note: it's said by some marks a spoken likeness heard in certain accents

parts.note: aren't means are not, that is do not exist

explanation.surface: Some people claim that Dickens's characters are not real.
explanation.walkthrough: Betsey Trotwood is David Copperfield's formidable relative in Dickens; in some accents 'aren't' rhymes with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Betsey Trotwood is the hero's great-aunt in David Copperfield, a female relative.

clue.text: Eastern member in public vehicle gets the message

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the word for the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a public transport vehicle
a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: A passenger with a foot in a streetcar receives a dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired dispatch was a common way to send a short message.

clue.text: 22 turned up with work for this old slave

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: 22-down is the ocean, another word for which is the sea
OP, short for opus, means a work

explanation.surface: Something from the deep surfaced, along with writing about an ancient bondsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SEA to AES in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist was traditionally said to have been a slave.

clue.text: Renounce it! Be a cad, anyway

indicators.note: anyway says the words before it may be taken in any order of letters

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to give up, behaving badly however they please.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a throne or a duty formally is to renounce it.

clue.text: Marshy land'll sound like this plant

indicators.note: sound like says the words before are matched to the answer by ear

parts.note: a fen is marshy land, so 'fen'll' is the contraction of fen will

explanation.surface: Boggy ground will apparently resemble a certain plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured herb is a garden plant.

clue.text: Refusal to move about in California in the small hours?

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: in places the word for moving about inside the California abbreviation

parts.note: to turn is to move about

explanation.surface: Someone declines to go roaming around California late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Something active at night, by extension, belongs to the small hours; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Weapon rejected in howitzer base

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weapon is turned down for use at an artillery base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run sitting inside 'howitzer base', and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry sword is a classic weapon.

clue.text: Cut short a dealer in costly textiles? Fine

indicators.note: cut short means the word for the dealer loses its final letter

parts.note: a mercer is a merchant in silks and other fine cloth

explanation.surface: A rich cloth merchant gets his bill trimmed, which is fine by him.
explanation.walkthrough: MERCER, a historic trader in silks and velvets, is docked its last R.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is an old legal verb for punishing with a monetary penalty.

clue.text: Tiny page could be a Cairene

indicators.note: could be invites the letters of the two words before it to become something else

explanation.surface: A small boy-servant might turn out to be from Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cairene is a native of Cairo, the capital of the North African country.

clue.text: Hood, for one, was more playful

definitions.meaning: Robin Hood, the legendary outlaw, was a famous bowman
arch means playfully mischievous, so its comparative

explanation.surface: Robin Hood was a cheekier fellow than most.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the best-known bowman of legend, and the comparative of arch means slyer or more teasing.

clue.text: It's less unusual to be a paying student

definitions.meaning: at Oxford, an undergraduate without a scholarship who pays fees

explanation.surface: Fee-paying students are more ordinary than scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford a student without a scholarship or exhibition, paying their own way, is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of ordinary-meaning common, and an Oxford fee-payer not on a scholarship.

clue.text: HQ dance profitable to Babe Ruth

parts.note: a headquarters is a base
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dance at headquarters made money for a famous sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the great New York Yankees slugger of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball sport was the game that made Babe Ruth rich and famous.

clue.text: Furnish French department from the balance

parts.note: to equip is to furnish with what is needed
the Oise is a department of northern France

explanation.surface: Someone fits out a French government office from the money left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Equilibrium, an even balance of weight or forces.

clue.text: A single column block

parts.note: a standing stone made of one solid piece, read as a pillar of one block

explanation.definitionFit: A single large stone, often a pillar or column, carved from one block.

clue.text: Control for party servant

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a minion is a lowly servant

explanation.surface: A party servant has been put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion is sovereignty or rule over a territory.

clue.text: Scottish surrogate deposited in river

indicators.note: in places the word for deposited inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a Scottish river
put means placed or deposited

explanation.surface: A Scottish stand-in was dumped in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage a depute is a deputy, someone acting on another's behalf.

clue.text: Uncommunicative about the purpose of an exhibition

indicators.note: about means the word for silent goes round the word for purpose

parts.note: mum means silent, not saying a word
use is purpose, as in 'what is the use?'

explanation.surface: Someone says nothing about why an exhibition is being held.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery of displayed objects is a place housing an exhibition, a loose but fair stand-in.

clue.text: Situation for one with a religious calling

definitions.text: Situation for one with a religious calling

parts.words: Situation for one with a religious calling
parts.note: a vocation suggests a priest, but this calling is the muezzin's cry to prayer, made from a mosque tower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious calling' looks like a vocation; it is literally the call to prayer, given from a mosque's tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender mosque tower is where the muezzin stands to call the faithful.

clue.text: Formal statement from adman to officer

parts.note: PRO, a public relations officer, is a publicity man much like an adman
taken as written
COL is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: An official statement passes from the advertising man to an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A protocol is a formal record or diplomatic document of agreed terms.

clue.text: The dark unfathom'd caves of —" (Gray)

parts.note: a quotation from Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, with the missing word to be supplied

explanation.definitionFit: Gray's line runs 'The dark unfathom'd caves of ... bear', the deep sea.

clue.text: Physical injury caused by the Ebro, perhaps?

definitions.text: Physical injury caused by the Ebro, perhaps?

parts.words: Physical injury caused by the Ebro, perhaps?
parts.note: the Ebro is a river in Spain, so the riddle reads as R (river) placed within SPAIN, giving a wrenched joint

explanation.walkthrough: No wordplay word marks the insertion: the Ebro is a river inside Spain, so R goes inside SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted ankle or wrist is a joint injury from overstretching the ligaments.

clue.text: A clever link-up of crucial importance

parts.note: cute can mean shrewd or clever

explanation.surface: A smart connection is vitally important.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute shortage or crisis is one that is severe and critical.

clue.text: Chap to write a yarn with no beginning or end

indicators.note: with no beginning or end strips the first and last letters from the word for the yarn

parts.note: cotton is a yarn spun from the cotton plant

explanation.surface: A man sets out to spin an endless tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to write' just joins; 'Chap' is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for any chap.

clue.text: Subject to a kind of song

definitions.meaning: the topic of an essay or talk
a signature tune for a film or show

explanation.surface: Someone is made to suffer a particular sort of song.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic under discussion, and the signature tune of a show, share the one word.

clue.text: Secret love initially repugnant to this conspirator

parts.note: an intrigue is a clandestine love affair

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word repugnant

explanation.surface: A hidden affair is distasteful to a plotter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter who schemes in secret is a conspirator.

clue.text: Religious installation involving ten men — not her!

indicators.note: involving here means the letters of the two phrases are tangled up together

explanation.surface: A church ceremony welcomes ten men and pointedly excludes a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Installing a bishop on his throne is a ceremonial religious installation.
